item.title: Ayu Sweetfish from the Nagara River — Guide
item.description: Ayu (sweetfish) from the Nagara River are a prized summer delicacy in Gifu, the clear, undammed river’s purity giving the fish a delicate, subtly sweet flavour and clean aroma that make Nagara ayu especially esteemed among Japanese food lovers. The most classic preparation is shioyaki, the whole fish skewered and salt-grilled over charcoal until the skin is crisp, eaten head to tail, and the ayu season, roughly summer, coincides with the river’s famous ukai cormorant fishing that traditionally caught them.

item.title: Nagara River Ukai: 1,300 Years of Cormorant Fishing — Guide
item.description: Ukai, or cormorant fishing, on the Nagara River near Gifu City is one of Japan’s most spectacular living traditions, practised for roughly 1,300 years, in which master fishermen (usho) in traditional grass skirts guide trained cormorants to dive for ayu sweetfish by the light of blazing baskets of fire hung from their boats. Held on summer nights, the fishing is watched from passenger viewing boats that drift alongside, and the usho of the Nagara River even hold a special imperial appointment, underlining the cultural importance of this atmospheric nighttime spectacle.

item.title: Nagara River Valley: One of Japan's Clearest Rivers — Guide
item.description: The Nagara River is counted among Japan’s three clearest rivers, flowing from the mountains of central Gifu through scenic gorges and green valleys on a largely undammed course that has kept its water exceptionally pure. This clarity supports the river’s famous ayu sweetfish and the centuries-old tradition of ukai cormorant fishing near Gifu City, while upstream the valley offers scenic drives, riverside walks and rafting, and the water itself is central to the culture and cuisine of the towns along its banks.
